points.what: North America orders fell 24.1% WoW, contributing -57 orders, 211.1% of the week's total change.
points.so_what: North America was the main region behind this week's order decline.

points.what: Search orders fell 4.3% WoW, contributing -27 orders, 100% of the week's total change.
points.so_what: Search, the largest traffic source, accounted for the entire net drop in orders this week.

points.what: Facebook orders rose 46.2% WoW, contributing +18 orders.
points.so_what: Gains in smaller channels like Facebook did not offset the declines from Search and North America.

points.what: AOV was $89.18, up 0.3% WoW and up 4.0% YoY.
points.so_what: Revenue per order kept growing, so the week's revenue shortfall reflects fewer orders rather than smaller baskets.

points.what: The cancellation rate fell to 14.5%, down 0.8pp WoW and down 0.9pp YoY.
points.so_what: With each percentage point of cancellations worth $787 in revenue, the lower rate points to less revenue lost to cancellations this week.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of 13 Apr 2026 rose to 11.4%, up 0.4pp WoW and up 1.0pp YoY.
points.so_what: Rising returns work against the gains from the lower cancellation rate, a quality trend worth watching.

points.what: New signups held flat at 238, up 8.7% YoY, while orders fell 3.0% WoW.
points.so_what: New customer growth did not slow even as this week's order volume declined.

summary.headline: Orders and revenue both fell behind target this week, with the year-to-date revenue pace also lagging at 94.6% of target.

points.what: Weekly orders reached 88.4% of target and weekly revenue reached 89.6% of target, both behind.
points.so_what: The week did not close the gap on either weekly measure, keeping pressure on the quarter's numbers.

points.what: Orders fell 3.0% and revenue fell 1.8% versus the prior week, both rated bad.
points.so_what: This reverses some of the recent weekly momentum going into the second month of the quarter.

points.what: Orders grew 73.6% YoY and revenue grew 82.4% YoY, against a target growth assumption of 75%.
points.so_what: Revenue growth is running ahead of the assumption behind this year's targets, while orders growth is just below it.

points.what: YTD revenue is at 94.6% of target and QTD revenue is at 98.4% of target, both behind.
points.so_what: The year overall remains further behind than the current quarter, keeping the annual target harder to reach.

points.what: The week finished at 88.4% of target for orders and 89.6% of target for revenue.
points.so_what: Both weekly measures fell short, adding to the gap that the quarter still needs to close.

points.what: QTD revenue is at 98.4% of target, a gap of $5,304, with 8 weeks left in the quarter.
points.so_what: Even with only a small dollar gap, the quarter remains behind target heading into the second half of Q2.

points.what: YTD revenue is at 94.6% of target, a gap of $59,788, with a required weekly run-rate of $81,319 for the rest of the year.
points.so_what: This required pace is well above the current 8-week run-rate of $62,467, so recent weeks are not yet matching what full-year attainment needs.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of 13 Apr 2026 rose to 11.4%, up 0.4pp WoW and up 1.0pp YoY, both rated bad.
points.so_what: A second straight increase points to a worsening order-quality trend not yet reflected in the cancellation rate.

points.what: The current 8-week revenue run-rate is $62,467, below the $81,319 weekly run-rate required for the rest of the year.
points.so_what: At the recent pace, the full-year revenue target is increasingly out of reach.

points.what: The quarter still needs $561,526 against the full-quarter target of $884,086, with 8 weeks left.
points.so_what: Reaching the full-quarter target now depends on stronger revenue than the pace seen in the quarter to date.
